title: Aeonglass
statementMd:
In the Euclidean plane, you are given a polygon $P=P_0P_1\cdots P_{n-1}$ whose vertices are listed in counterclockwise order.

An angle $\alpha$ ($0 \le \alpha \lt \pi$) is a **stable direction** if and only if there exists a $c \in R$ such that, for every point $X$ in polygon $P$ (including its boundary), the perpendicular segment from $X$ to the line $$ \cos \alpha\,x + \sin \alpha\,y + c = 0 $$ lies entirely in $P$ (including its boundary). Here $\alpha$ is a direction of the line's normal vector.

Find the number of **stable directions**. This number can be shown to be finite.

## Input

The first line contains an integer $T$ ($1 \le T \le 100$), the number of test cases.

The first line of each test case contains an integer $n$ ($3 \le n \le 10^5$), the number of polygon vertices.

Each of the next $n$ lines contains two integers $x_i,y_i$ ($-10^9 \le x_i,y_i \le 10^9$), the coordinates of the $i$-th vertex, listed in counterclockwise order.

Within a test case, all vertices are distinct. Adjacent edges intersect only at their shared endpoint, and nonadjacent edges do not intersect.

The sum of $n$ over all test cases does not exceed $10^5$.

## Output

For each test case, output one integer: the number of **stable directions**.

## Note

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/7244693a621ef4fd9f62c24a11181dc9cb8c9812.png)

The lines and **stable directions** for test case 1 are

$$ \begin{aligned} L_1:\quad &x-1=0, &\alpha_1&=0,\\ L_2:\quad &\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}x+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}y-\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{4}=0, &\alpha_2&=\frac{\pi}{4},\\ L_3:\quad &-\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}x+\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}y=0, &\alpha_3&=\pi-\arctan 2. \end{aligned} $$

The lines and **stable directions** for test case 2 are

$$ \begin{aligned} L_1:\quad &x-1=0, &\alpha_1&=0,\\ L_2:\quad &y-1=0, &\alpha_2&=\frac{\pi}{2},\\ L_3:\quad &\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}x+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}y-\sqrt{2}=0, &\alpha_3&=\frac{\pi}{4},\\ L_4:\quad &-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}x+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}y=0, &\alpha_4&=\frac{3\pi}{4}. \end{aligned} $$

The line and **stable direction** for test case 3 are

$$ L:\quad x-\frac{1}{2}=0, \qquad \alpha_1=0. $$

The corresponding line is not uniquely determined.
